articles.title: Anger or fear? Dogs may be able to read it on your face
articles.snippet: Brain scans offer the first evidence that dogs can read certain human facial expressions.
articles.summary: Brain scans show the first evidence that dogs can read certain human facial expressions. This research suggests dogs might be able to tell the difference between emotions like anger and fear on people's faces.

articles.title: These clues might point to life on other worlds
articles.snippet: Gases and color on distant planets may trace to activity by extraterrestrial life. If so, those E.T.s are likely tiny, one-celled beings.
articles.summary: Gases and color on distant planets might be clues pointing to tiny, one-celled extraterrestrial life. If these signs are real, they suggest that alien beings do exist out there.

articles.title: Some germs ride a superhighway at the edge of space
articles.snippet: Some microbes common on Earth’s surface lead a secret double life. Soaring higher than jumbo jets, they carry clues about disease spread and alien life.
articles.summary: Some common Earth microbes soar higher than jumbo jets into the edge of space and lead secret double lives. These high-flying germs carry important clues about how diseases spread and what alien life might be like.
